fact: The article names Tunisia's National Digital Strategy 2021-2025 as a five-year plan; its stated period had ended by the article's date, and the article gives no successor strategy by name (only a 'broader national vision for 2026-2030'); the as-at date is the article's publication date (2026-03-09). Text public: not stated

The article says the Digital Strategy 2021-2025 'translated vision into delivery', citing by 2025 nearly 80% of the population as internet users and 4G coverage near 95%, measured against no target of the strategy itself and with no published progress report named.

The EBRD board report says the Tunisian Government 'has launched' the National Digital Strategy 2021-2025; no adopting act or body beyond 'the Government' is named, and the launch date is not given, so the date is the report's (2024-07-24).

The report gives the National Digital Strategy 2021-2025 a stated period of 2021-2025, which includes the report's date of 2024-07-24; it neither links nor quotes the text from an official site. Text public: not stated

The paper (Africa Policy Research Institute, 2024) says the Plan National Stratégique Tunisie Digitale 2020 was extended to 2025 because of insufficient progress, and the extended plan is called the Digital Tunisia Plan; the 2024 as-of date is the paper's year, as the document gives no other date. Text public: not stated.

The ITU repository lists the National Digital Strategic Plan / Digital Tunisia as the country's strategy and says the countries it lists have adopted one; no adopting act is named, so this is dated by the repository's 2025 publication year.
The repository gives the time frame of the National Digital Strategic Plan / Digital Tunisia as 2017 - 2020 and 2022 - 2025.
The repository names the Ministry of Communication Technologies as lead/owner of the National Digital Strategic Plan / Digital Tunisia.

The ministry's October 2018 presentation sets the Stratégie Tunisie Digitale 2020 targets for 2020 (100% of homes connected, 13,500 MTND digital value added, 5,000 MTND digital exports) after a five-year plan started in 2015.

The presentation lists an implementation plan with dated 2018 and 2020 targets per axis (infrastructure, e-government, e-business, Smart Tunisia) and a selection of named projects; it states no costs.

The ministry's 'Réalisations et objectifs' table gives 2014-2017 outturns against the strategy's targets for digital value added, digital exports, jobs created, connected homes and mobile broadband penetration (e.g. 44.5% of homes connected in 2017 against 100% for 2020), with several 2017 values marked ND; it covers some axes only.

The presentation's governance chart gives the CSEN (Conseil stratégique de l'économie numérique) the validation of the strategy, arbitration and recommendations to support implementation, above a steering committee and per-programme project offices in the ministries.
